architecture.text:
PART 1 — ARCHITECTURE SUMMARY (plain text, no markdown bold):

PRODUCT IDENTITY
- Headline: "Every organisation is accountable for the impact it creates on society. Most are still flying blind."
- One-line pitch: "SAIGE brings Sustainability, ESG, SDGs, EHS, and CSR into one unified enterprise impact intelligence platform."

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE
- The page's primary goal is to capture early access sign-ups via a gated waitlist form, converting visitors into founding members ahead of the full platform launch. A secondary objective is to establish credibility through problem-framing statistics and a live animated demo, nudging hesitant visitors toward the demo as a lower-commitment entry point.

INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE
- 1. Hero / Above-the-fold: Launch announcement banner, headline statement, platform description, link to white paper, and toggle showing demo vs. full platform scope.
- 2. Live Demo Animation: Auto-cycling org-type simulator displaying EIP scores, domain confidence percentages, and sector averages across nine organisation types.
- 3. Problem / Why SAIGE Matters: Four statistics from named sources (KPMG, MIT Sloan, Deloitte, Gartner) followed by domain counts, frameworks supported, and org-type use cases with a single beta testimonial.
- 4. Value Proposition / Without vs. With SAIGE: Side-by-side contrast of manual legacy workflows versus the unified SAIGE platform, covering reporting speed, scoring, and compliance framework coverage.
- 5. About, Early Access Form, and Footer: Founder bio, company provenance, early access sign-up form with role and org-type selectors, proprietary IP notice, and navigation links.

CONTENT INVENTORY
- Visible CTAs: "Join the Early Access List →", "Read the full White Paper →", "What does this demo show vs. the full platform?", "Request Early Access →", "Explore the Demo →", "LinkedIn Profile", "Send Message", "Full Platform (Coming Soon)"
- Visible forms or input affordances: One contact/question form (unlabelled fields, submit labeled "Send Message"); one early access registration form with fields for Work Email, Organisation Name, Role (dropdown: Board/C-Suite, Sustainability Lead, EHS Manager, Analyst/Practitioner, Other), and Organisation Type (dropdown: School/University, Local Government, Gov. Agency, Business/Manufacturing, NGO/Nonprofit, Other), submitted via "Request Early Access →".
- Trust signals: KPMG Global ESG Survey 2024 statistic (68% ESG reports contain material errors); MIT Sloan 2024 statistic (73% of sustainability leaders cite fragmented data); Deloitte Insights 2024 statistic (40% compliance cost reduction in 18 months); Gartner 2024 statistic (6+ disconnected tools average); one named beta testimonial attributed to "Sustainability Director, Manufacturing (Beta)"; founder credential "Victor Udo, FNSE, PhD, 35+ Years Experience"; framework names GRI, CSRD, TCFD, ISO 45001, UN SDGs cited as built-in; AASHE STARS referenced for university use case.

TECH SIGNALS
- Page is JS-rendered (confirmed by capture method: browserless), indicating a JavaScript-heavy frontend, likely React, Vue, or a similar SPA framework given the auto-cycling animation component and dynamic org-type selector.
- Auto-cycling demo with 3-second interval and click-to-jump behaviour suggests client-side state management (React useState/useEffect or equivalent).
- No CDN, hosting provider, or build tool is explicitly identifiable from the body text alone, but the demo domain (saigedemo.com) is separate from the production domain (SaigePlatform.com), suggesting a staged environment strategy.
- No explicit references to analytics tags, cookie banners, or third-party script loaders visible in the captured content.
- Copyright year listed as 2026, which is anomalous and may indicate a placeholder or forward-dated IP notice rather than a technical error.

ACCESSIBILITY SIGNALS
- Heading hierarchy shows a non-standard pattern: h1 is present and meaningful, but h3 elements ("High Level SAIGE Animation", "Why SAIGE Matters", "Be among the first to use SAIGE on your own data") appear before or without intervening h2s in some sections, suggesting heading levels are used for visual styling rather than strict semantic structure.
- Two h2 elements are present ("Five sources consolidated. One score. One platform." and "Built by people who understand the problem.") and are semantically appropriate for section delineation.
- No alt-text for images is visible in the captured body text; emoji characters are used as visual icons (e.g., for org types) without confirmed accessible labels.
- Contrast indicators are not determinable from text capture alone, but the use of coloured status indicators (e.g., "🔴 Developing") without accompanying text descriptions beyond the label may present issues for colour-blind users.
- Form fields include asterisk-marked required fields (Work Email, Organisation Name) but no visible error messaging or ARIA hints are indicated in the captured content.

QUALITY SCORE: 71/100
- The page demonstrates strong conceptual clarity and a coherent narrative structure with credible third-party statistics, but its pre-launch status, missing production evidence, non-standard heading hierarchy, unverifiable form functionality, a forward-dated copyright year, and absence of confirmed alt-text or accessibility affordances meaningfully limit its overall completeness and credibility score.

improvement_plan.text:
PART 1 — IMPROVEMENT PLAN (plain text, no markdown bold):

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The single biggest opportunity is converting the strong conceptual narrative and credible third-party statistics into actual sign-ups by reducing friction and ambiguity around the early access form, which currently competes with too many CTAs and lacks urgency signals tied to a concrete launch date. The single biggest risk is credibility erosion: a pre-launch demo site with a forward-dated 2026 copyright, no visible social proof beyond one anonymised testimonial, no cookie/privacy consent mechanism, and a separate production domain that does not yet exist (SaigePlatform.com) collectively signals vaporware to a sceptical enterprise buyer evaluating a compliance-sensitive product.

PRIORITIZED IMPROVEMENTS (max 7)

P0 | trust | Fix-or-explain the 2026 copyright year — A forward-dated copyright year on a pre-launch site reads as an error to enterprise procurement teams who screenshot footers during due diligence; change it to the current year or add a parenthetical such as "(founded 2024, platform launching 2026)" to contextualise the intent deliberately.

P0 | conversion | Consolidate CTAs to a single primary action per viewport — The page presents at least eight distinct calls to action simultaneously (Join Early Access, Read White Paper, What does this demo show, Request Early Access, Explore the Demo, Send Message, LinkedIn Profile, Full Platform Coming Soon), which splits attention and reduces the probability of any single conversion; audit and suppress all secondary CTAs below the fold until after the primary form is passed, leaving one visible CTA at each scroll depth.

P0 | compliance | Add a visible cookie consent banner and link a real Privacy Policy — SAIGE's target buyers are sustainability and ESG leaders who are acutely aware of GDPR, CCPA, and CSRD compliance obligations; operating a form-capture page without an active consent mechanism and a functional Privacy Policy link (currently a dead or placeholder link) directly undermines the product's credibility claim as a compliance platform, and creates legal exposure in EU and California-regulated markets.

P1 | trust | Replace the single anonymised beta testimonial with two or three richer, named or role-attributed quotes including organisation size and sector — "Sustainability Director, Manufacturing (Beta)" provides no verifiable signal to an enterprise buyer; even adding a job title, company headcount tier, and country of operation substantially increases believability without requiring a named logo release.

P1 | copy | Add a concrete launch timeline or milestone indicator near the hero — "Coming Soon" and "Full Production Launch Coming Soon" without a quarter, month, or at minimum a year creates uncertainty that pushes risk-averse enterprise evaluators away; a statement such as "Onboarding founding members from Q3 2025 — [X] organisations already on the list" combines urgency, social proof, and timeline in one sentence.

P1 | technical | Instrument form submissions with analytics and confirm server-side delivery — No analytics tags, form success states, or error handling are visible in the captured content; without confirmed event tracking on both the early access form and the contact form, the team cannot measure conversion rate, identify drop-off fields, or validate that submitted emails are being received, making all optimisation efforts unmeasurable.

P2 | compliance | Repair heading hierarchy to follow a strict h1 → h2 → h3 sequence throughout — Multiple h3 elements appear without a parent h2 in the DOM, which harms screen-reader navigation and fails WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships); restructure section headings so every h3 is nested under a semantically appropriate h2, and replace emoji-only org-type icons with emoji plus aria-label attributes.

QUICK WINS (max 3)

Change the copyright year from 2026 to 2025 (or add a bracketed launch-year note) — this is a one-line text edit that immediately removes a credibility red flag visible to every visitor who reads the footer.

Add a waitlist counter or founding-member count next to the "Request Early Access" button, such as "Join 142 organisations already on the list" — this is a single line of copy (even if seeded with a modest real number) that introduces social proof at the exact moment of conversion decision and takes under 30 minutes to ship as a static string.

Make the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use footer links point to real, populated pages rather than placeholder targets — even a minimal one-page policy drafted from a standard template eliminates a compliance objection and is achievable in under an hour using a policy generator service.

STRUCTURAL CHANGES (max 3)

Redesign the hero section to use a two-column layout that places the animated EIP demo directly beside the early access form above the fold — currently the demo and the form are separated by multiple scroll depths, meaning a visitor who finds the demo compelling must scroll significantly to act on that interest; co-locating the demo and the sign-up form in a single above-the-fold panel is a structural layout change that requires design and front-end engineering work but directly addresses the gap between engagement and conversion.

Build a persistent sticky header CTA bar that collapses the full form into a single "Get Early Access" button that expands inline or opens a modal — this ensures the primary conversion action is always one click away regardless of scroll position, requires a modal/drawer component and scroll-event logic, and prevents the user from having to hunt for the form after being persuaded mid-page.

Implement a segmented onboarding flow triggered by the Organisation Type dropdown selection, so that after a visitor selects their org type (e.g., NGO, Local Government) the surrounding page copy, use case callout, and demo org type dynamically update to match their context — this is a meaningful personalisation feature that requires state-management work but directly addresses the multi-segment audience problem (nine org types listed) by making every visitor feel the platform was built for them specifically.

QUALITY SCORE: 78/100
The input architecture summary is detailed and well-structured, providing sufficient signal on IA, CTAs, trust indicators, tech stack, and accessibility to generate grounded recommendations. The score is capped below 85 because the capture is text-only with no visual layout data, no confirmed analytics baseline, no live form-test results, and no access to actual conversion metrics, meaning several recommendations (particularly around CTA placement and form friction) are directionally sound but cannot be precisely calibrated without heatmap or session data.
